settings.label: My Domain URL
settings.meaning: The org's own address: the token and every API call go to it.
settings.whereToFind: Setup › My Domain: the Current My Domain URL, https://<name>.my.salesforce.com. For test, a sandbox's, https://<name>--<sandbox>.sandbox.my.salesforce.com. Not login.salesforce.com: the client credentials flow needs the org's own domain. Salesforce's keys look the same in a sandbox and in production, so nothing here is checked per environment.

settings.label: Consumer key
settings.meaning: Names the app's External Client App to Salesforce.
settings.whereToFind: Setup › External Client App Manager › the app › Settings › OAuth Settings: Consumer Key. In the app's OAuth settings, Enable Client Credentials Flow; in its policies, set Run As to an integration user, whose access is all the app gets. In the sandbox's own app for test.

settings.label: Consumer secret
settings.meaning: Proves the token request comes from the app.
settings.whereToFind: Next to the consumer key: Setup › External Client App Manager › the app › Settings › OAuth Settings: Consumer Secret.

settings.label: API version
settings.meaning: The REST API version every call uses. Leave it unset for v68.0 (Winter '27); pin another only to match code written for it.
settings.whereToFind: A version the org lists at <My Domain URL>/services/data/, such as v68.0.

settings.label: Flow webhook secret
settings.meaning: Checks that a call to the app's webhook came from the org's flow. Salesforce signs nothing it sends: the flow sends this secret in a header.
settings.whereToFind: A long random string of your own, kept in the org as an External Credential's custom header (X-Webhook-Secret) that the flow's HTTP callout uses.

operations.name: oauth.token
operations.purpose: Gets an access token by the client credentials flow, as the app's Run As user. There's no refresh token: a new one is asked for when a call answers 401.

operations.name: contacts.create

operations.purpose: Reads one Contact by id, optionally only some fields.

operations.purpose: Deletes one Contact (to the Recycle Bin).

operations.name: contacts.upsert

operations.name: soql.query
operations.purpose: Runs a SOQL query and returns its first page of records, with the locator of the next.

operations.name: soql.queryMore
operations.purpose: Reads the next page of a query by the nextRecordsUrl its previous page gave.

operations.name: composite.execute
operations.purpose: Runs up to 25 subrequests in one call, all or none: a later one can use an earlier one's id (@{ref.id}), and any failure rolls back the lot.

signature.description: Salesforce has no signed webhooks. A record-triggered flow posts JSON to the app with an HTTP callout whose External Credential adds the header X-Webhook-Secret: the shared secret. The app compares it with the setting in constant time. The secret doesn't cover the body, so it's only sent over HTTPS; a delivery is deduplicated on a digest of its raw body.

events.meaning: The flow saw a record change. The body's event field says which (contact.updated): the flow chooses it.
